news.title: Iran Intensifies Hormuz Tanker Attacks Just as Oil Prices Slide
news.summary: Strikes on tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz are becoming more frequent even as crude prices ease on plentiful Middle East supply.
news.why: Falling oil prices may not translate into cheaper freight while war-risk premiums and tanker security costs keep climbing on Gulf routes.

news.title: TARA GAS Burning Off Oman as Another Tanker Attack Leaves 11 Injured
news.summary: An LPG carrier hit near the Strait of Hormuz was still on fire and drifting, according to a fresh navigational warning, after another attack that injured 11 people.
news.why: Importers relying on Gulf-sourced LPG and petrochemicals should expect continued delays, rerouting and higher insurance surcharges.

news.title: As logistics operators and shippers look to 2027, high costs, constant disruption, and uncertainty roil their plans
news.summary: Armstrong & Associates projects U.S. third-party logistics revenue climbing about 6.7% to roughly $375 billion in 2027, against a backdrop of record diesel and Gulf and Red Sea disruptions adding up to two weeks to some transits.
news.why: Shippers budgeting for 2027 should plan for sustained cost inflation from 3PLs and longer ocean lead times rather than a return to normal.

news.title: DOL sticks with independent contractor proposal, trucking applauds
news.summary: The Labor Department finalized its independent contractor rule largely as proposed in February, with the change taking effect 60 days after publication and drawing support from major trucking groups.
news.why: Clearer rules on owner-operator status reduce legal risk for carriers that rely on contractors, which helps keep truckload capacity and pricing stable.

news.title: Panama Files Criminal Complaint Tied to CK Hutchison Ports Dispute
news.summary: Panama's comptroller has taken legal action over irregularities an audit found in a state concession held by a CK Hutchison port subsidiary.
news.why: Escalating legal fights over terminals at both ends of the Panama Canal add uncertainty for shippers routing cargo through those gateways.

news.title: Honda invests $462M in Alabama plant to boost production
news.summary: Honda is putting $462 million into its Alabama assembly plant to expand output of its best-selling models.
news.why: More U.S.-built vehicle volume signals growing demand for local parts suppliers and a continued shift away from imported components.

news.title: How Home Depot built the missing logistics piece for its Pro business
news.summary: Home Depot combined flatbed distribution centers, acquisitions and new technology to give contractor customers faster, more reliable jobsite deliveries.
news.why: Distributors selling bulky goods to trade buyers can see how dedicated last-mile networks become a competitive edge over price alone.

news.title: How Brooks Running is using supplier data to address human rights risks
news.summary: The footwear brand runs a yearly simulated customs detention with its suppliers to test how well it can trace materials and prove compliance.
news.why: Importers exposed to forced-labor enforcement can borrow the drill to find documentation gaps before a real shipment is held at the border.

news.title: Oil Traders in Talks With QatarEnergy for Long-Term Supplies
news.summary: Large commodity trading houses are negotiating term contracts for more Qatari crude after playing a big role in moving Gulf oil during the Iran-U.S. conflict.
news.why: Traders locking in long-term Gulf volumes suggests they expect the region's supply risk to persist, which keeps energy-linked freight costs volatile.

news.title: U.S. Holds Historic Deep-Sea Mining Lease Sale
news.summary: The first U.S. auction of offshore critical-mineral leases drew about $6 million in winning bids across more than 31.5 million acres of seabed.
news.why: Low bids show seabed minerals are a long-term bet, so buyers of battery and electronics metals should not count on new domestic supply soon.

news.title: Rockwell Automation buys Agilox to combine AMR fleets
news.summary: Rockwell is acquiring Austrian autonomous forklift maker Agilox to pair its pallet-moving robots with Rockwell's existing OTTO mobile robots.
news.why: Warehouse operators evaluating automation may soon get mixed robot fleets from one vendor, simplifying integration but increasing supplier lock-in.

news.title: Can Humanoid Robots Earn Their Keep on the Factory Floor?
news.summary: Analysts expect very few companies to move humanoid robot pilots into real production before 2028, with only around 7,000 sold last year compared with hundreds of thousands of conventional industrial robots.
news.why: Operations leaders should prioritize proven arms and mobile robots for near-term labor gaps and treat humanoids as an experiment, not a plan.

news.title: Jim Beam won't resume production at flagship distillery next year
news.summary: Suntory is shifting Jim Beam output to a different Kentucky site as demand weakens for lower-priced spirits.
news.why: Suppliers of grain, barrels and packaging to the spirits industry should prepare for lower volumes and consolidated production footprints.

news.title: China Oilfield Services Orders 59 Offshore Vessels in $1.6 Billion Shipbuilding Deal
news.summary: COSL has contracted three Chinese yards to build 59 offshore support vessels for about $1.64 billion.
news.why: Large domestic orders tighten Chinese shipyard capacity, which can push up newbuild prices and delivery times for other buyers.
